components.css: .ds-panel { background: oklch(0.962 0.013 220); border-radius: 24px; padding: 40px; font-family: Vazirmatn, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-window { max-width: 384px; background: oklch(0.985 0.005 220); border-radius: 24px; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px oklch(0.21 0.025 245 / 0.1), 0 8px 10px -6px oklch(0.21 0.025 245 / 0.1); } .ds-window-bar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 16px 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid oklch(0.9 0.015 225); } .ds-window-title { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: oklch(0.21 0.025 245); } .ds-window-meta { font-size: 0.75rem; color: oklch(0.46 0.025 240); } .ds-window-row { display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: center; padding: 14px 24px; } .ds-well { width: 36px; height: 36px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 14px; background: oklch(0.93 0.025 222); } .ds-row-title { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: oklch(0.21 0.025 245); }

components.css: .ds-pillar { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; max-width: 280px; padding: 32px; border-radius: 24px; background: oklch(0.955 0.03 160); color: oklch(0.21 0.025 245); font-family: Vazirmatn, system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 300ms ease; } .ds-pillar:hover, .ds-pillar:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 10px 40px -10px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); } .ds-pillar:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.5 0.1 232); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-pillar-well { width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 16px; background: oklch(0.985 0.005 220 / 0.7); } .ds-pillar-title { font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-pillar-text { font-size: 1rem; line-height: 2; color: oklch(0.46 0.025 240); }

narrative.overview:
A good workshop in daylight: wide benches, every tool on its hook, each team's work laid out where the manager can see it. Nothing is hidden and nothing is shouting. The visitor is a technology lead deciding whether AI can join the daily work of every team, and the page should feel like walking through that workshop: real work in progress, clearly arranged, with the controls in plain sight.

The structure follows dust.tt, the reference the owner pinned: a bright open canvas, large confident headings, short copy, one idea per section, soft colored panels, real product UI resting on those panels, tabs by team, numbered pillars and one dark closing band. The product is the picture. Real screenshots of GodarChat and the admin panel, framed as windows on calm tinted panels, carry the argument; decorative illustration does not.

The system is product-centered and alive: motion shows an assistant doing work (a message arriving, a tool call completing, a cost meter settling) rather than decorating the page. Persian and right-to-left are the home language of every decision, and light and dark themes are equal citizens.
keyCharacteristics: Dust's structure and clarity, in Persian, right to left.
Real product screenshots in window frames on soft colored panels; the product is the hero image.
A small family of calm pastel panels, one per differentiator, all at the same lightness.
One steady blue accent for actions; neutrals tinted cool.
Cards lift slightly off the bench with soft shadows.
Motion that demonstrates work, never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Matched Lightness Rule
rules.body: Differentiator panels change hue, never lightness or chroma. Side by side they read as one family; none may outshout another.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Steady Blue is the only saturated color on the page. Panels are tinted, never saturated, and are never used for text or buttons.

rules.name: The Color Means a Promise Rule
rules.body: Each differentiator keeps its panel color on every page it appears. A panel color is not chosen for variety.

rules.name: The No Tracking Rule
rules.body: Never apply negative or positive letter-spacing to Persian text; it breaks Arabic-script joining.

rules.name: The Quiet Heading Rule
rules.body: One weight step above body is enough; size carries the hierarchy, not stacked bold, color and caps. No eyebrows above headings; numbering only where the sequence carries meaning.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with Workshop Ink and offset downward. No zero-offset glows, no hard offset shadows, no glass or backdrop blur.

dos: Do show the real product: real screenshots in Product Windows on tinted panels.
Do keep each differentiator on its own panel color everywhere it appears.
Do use motion to demonstrate an assistant's work, once, on entry, and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do build and check every section in light and dark themes.
Do build pages from the shared patterns in `app/components/patterns` (live samples at `/_patterns`) and the `site-*` / `tone-*` utilities; never raw palette colors.
donts: Don't use water, ford or river illustration, ripples or wave motifs; that world is retired.
Don't introduce a second saturated color or use a panel tint for text or buttons.
Don't use indigo, slate or other raw Tailwind palette colors; feature pages that still do are debt to migrate.
Don't apply letter-spacing to Persian text.
Don't present invented numbers, logos or quotes inside mocks as real.
Don't use glass, glows, gradients on text, or decorative blobs.
